author: blu
body: A grant has three parts and the process table has a slot for each: the capability word at offset 56 says what the process may do, the filesystem scope at offset 64 says what path it may name, and the network scope at offset 24 says what authority it may reach. Writing the capability word without a scope hands a loaded binary its authority and loses the limit on it -- a program whose manifest said "filesystem read, under /config/" would run with filesystem read over the whole volume, and one that said "network write, to api.example.com" would run able to POST anywhere. So apply-load-decision writes ALL THREE, and a denied decision writes NONE.

author: blu
body: Each scope goes through its process-set-*-scope helper rather than a poke because a Text is a pointer and the process table wants that pointer, not its bytes; the helpers are privileged (cap-capability-admin), which is the point -- installing a scope is the loader's business and not an application's.

author: blu
body: The bare `True` that used to end this act block cannot come back: a literal on its own line after an act-bind is parsed as an ARGUMENT to the line above it (CDX1070), not as the block's result. The block ends in an application instead, and wired-ok is what makes that application an honest one.
